{{Short description|São Toméan biologist and politician (born 1961)}}
'''Maria de Jesus Trovoada dos Santos''' (born 1961) is a São Tomé and Príncipe biologist and politician who is known for her research on human genetics. She was appointed Minister of Health to the [[Government of São Tomé and Príncipe|XVI Constitutional Government of São Tomé and Príncipe]] in 2014.

== Career ==
Maria de Jesus Trovoada dos Santos was born on 25 December 1961 in the parish of Conceição, São Tomé and Príncipe.<ref>Barros, Joana (2009). ''[https://www.viveraciencia.org/images/PDFs/Maria%20Jesus%20Trovoada_Excerto.pdf Lives to Discover: Women Scientists from the Lusophone World] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240629024652/https://www.viveraciencia.org/images/PDFs/Maria%20Jesus%20Trovoada_Excerto.pdf |date=2024-06-29 }}'' (PDF) . [SL]: Themes and Debates</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-02-08 |title=Portugal Protocolo Nº40 {{!}} 2018 by PORTUGAL PROTOCOLO REVISTA - Issuu |url=https://issuu.com/portugalprotocolo/docs/portugal_protocolo_40_2018 |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=issuu.com |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=July 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> After she graduated from secondary school, she worked as a teacher and volunteered with education programmes that aimed to improve the health of agricultural workers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2021-05-15 |title=Maria de Jesus Trovoada :: Cimeira-femina-summit |url=https://cimeira-femina-summit.webnode.pt/maria-de-jesus-trovoada/ |access-date=2023-10-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515194703/https://cimeira-femina-summit.webnode.pt/maria-de-jesus-trovoada/ |archive-date=2021-05-15 }}</ref>

In 1984, she left for Angola where she began to study Biology at the [[University of Luanda]], which she went on to complete at the [[University of Coimbra]], Portugal.<ref name=":1" /> She stayed in Portugal until 2010, when she returned to São Tomé and Príncipe. During her time in Portugal she worked as a researcher at the [[Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciência]], where she focused on studying the genetic susceptibility of São Toméans to [[malaria]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Neto |first=Ricardo |date=2018-09-18 |title=Ministra da Saúde, Maria de Jesus Trovoada, eleita Prémio Femina 2018 |url=https://www.stp-press.st/2018/09/18/ministra-da-saude-maria-jesus-trovoada-eleita-premio-femina-2018/ |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=STP-PRESS |language=pt-PT}}</ref>

Returning to São Tomé and Príncipe, she headed the National Program to Fight Malaria at the country's National Center for Endemic Diseases.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-04-25 |title=São Tomé: Revés na luta contra oa malária |url=https://www.voaportugues.com/a/article-04-15-12-stp-malaria-148922245/1451367.html |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=VOA |language=pt |archive-date=2023-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130050307/https://www.voaportugues.com/a/article-04-15-12-stp-malaria-148922245/1451367.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In her scientific work she has focused on studying the genetic characteristics of human populations, residing in the São Tomé archipelago and in central Portugal.<ref name=":0" /> Research projects have included: the study of population samples looking for genetic [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphisms]] in newborns and the development of electrophoretic separation techniques, amongst others.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

In 2014, she joined the XVI Constitutional Government of São Tomé and Príncipe, assuming the position of Minister of Health.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Heath-Brown |first=Nick |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lDkUDgAAQBAJ&dq=Maria+de+Jesus+Trovoada&pg=PA1043 |title=The Statesman's Yearbook 2016: The Politics, Cultures and Economies of the World |date=2017-02-07 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-349-57823-8 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Lansford |first=Tom |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VCFoDwAAQBAJ&dq=Maria+de+Jesus+Trovoada&pg=PA537 |title=Political Handbook of the World 2018-2019 |date=2019-03-19 |publisher=CQ Press |isbn=978-1-5443-2711-2 |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Matriz Portuguesa (Association for the Development of Culture and Knowledge) awarded her the Femina Prize in 2018''.''<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-18 |title=Prémio Femina 2018 :: Premio-Femina |url=https://premio-femina8.webnode.pt/premio-femina-2018/ |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=premio-femina8.webnode.pt |language=pt}}</ref>

A biography of her was published in the book ''Vidas a Descobrir: Mulheres Cientistas do Mundo Lusophone (''Associação Viver a Ciência, 2009).<ref>{{Cite web |title="Vidas a Descobrir – Mulheres Cientistas do Mundo Lusófono" |url=https://www.viveraciencia.org/pt/aspublicacoes/livros/livro-vidas-a-descobrir |access-date=2023-10-08 |website=www.viveraciencia.org |archive-date=2023-09-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230921230612/https://viveraciencia.org/pt/aspublicacoes/livros/livro-vidas-a-descobrir |url-status=live }}</ref>
